It's thought that each vocalisation is used to communicate different things. 2. They are protective over their kill.  Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. Tigers primarily hunt deer, but as opportunistic predators, they can also eat wild boars, birds, fish, rodents, amphibians, reptiles, and even insects. Footage shows a trainer attempting to manage two tigers in the ring when one of them suddenly leaps over the protective barrier and into the audience seating area. Spectators, including many families with young children, were seen panicking and scrambling for safety as the animal moved through the stands. Circus director Nikolai Dovgaluk confirmed that the situation was safely resolved without any injuries after a trainer successfully collared the tiger and returned it to its cage.
